reason: The composite abstain interpretation retains nonattachment and required abstention together. Both candidate annotations now match the prevailing position, so these entries are excluded from the active contradiction ledger. Original grades, source excerpts and alternative-position evidence are preserved below without regrading.

entries.note: al-Qāḍī in al-Jāmiʿ calls the lot qiyās al-madhhab; Taqī al-Dīn reads Aḥmad's words (Ṣāliḥ) as pointing to both falling; abstention is by Aḥmad's naṣṣ (ʿAbd Allāh).

evidence.excerpt_ar: أحدهما خطأ الآخر، في أصح الوجهين فيهما، نقل ابن القاسم " فليتقيا الشبهة
evidence.note: Al-Inṣāf (fāʾida under the raven case) says neither wife is divorced but intercourse is forbidden to both men unless one believes the other is wrong, "fī aṣaḥḥ al-wajhayn fīhimā". The preceding line reads "lam taṭluqā, wa-yaḥrumu ʿalayhimā al-waṭʾ, illā maʿa iʿtiqād", which is the abstention view of Aḥmad's naṣṣ (Ibn al-Qāsim: "fa-l-yattaqiyā al-shubha").

evidence.excerpt_ar: الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ الآخر، في الأصح فيهما، نقل ابن القاسم
evidence.note: Al-Furūʿ rules that intercourse is forbidden to both unless one believes the other is wrong, "fī al-aṣaḥḥ fīhimā", while the marriages remain.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ولم يعلما لم تطلقا ولم تعتقا ويحرم عليهما الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ
evidence.note: The Muntahā states decisively that neither wife is divorced but intercourse is forbidden to both unless one believes the other wrong, so each abstains.

evidence.excerpt_ar: الطائر غرابا أم غيره (لم تطلقا) أي زوجتاهما (ولم تعتقا) أي أمتاهما ; لأن
evidence.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā rules that neither wife is divorced, since the one who broke his oath is unknown and each one's certainty of marriage remains, with maintenance still owed.

evidence.excerpt_ar: والشيخ تقي الدين - رحمه الله - وقوع الطلاق، وجزم به في الروضة، فيقرع،
evidence.note: Al-Inṣāf adds al-Ḥulwānī, his son (al-Tabṣira), Taqī al-Dīn and al-Rawḍa to the holders of "divorce falls, so lots are drawn". Al-Qāḍī called this the manṣūṣ.

entries.note: «وقياس المنصوص ههنا أن يكف كل واحد عن وطء أمته».

evidence.excerpt_ar: ولم يعلما لم تطلقا ولم تعتقا ويحرم عليهما الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ
evidence.note: The Muntahā rules that neither slave-woman is freed but intercourse with them is forbidden to both owners unless one believes the other is wrong, which is the qiyās al-manṣūṣ that each abstains.

evidence.excerpt_ar: يعلماه لم تعتقا ولم تطلق وحرم عليها الوطء إلا مع اعتقاد أحدهما خطأ الآخر
evidence.note: The Iqnāʿ likewise says the slave-women are not freed and intercourse is forbidden unless one believes the other is wrong.

evidence.excerpt_ar: لم تعتقا) أي الأمتان (ولم تطلقا) أي المرأتان، لأن الحانث منهما ليس معلوما
evidence.note: Kashshāf explains that the two slave-women are not freed because the one who broke his oath is unknown, and no ruling falls on either man individually.

evidence.excerpt_ar: حر، ولم يعلماه، فلا عتق، فإن اشترى أحدهما عبد الآخر فقيل: يعتق أحدهما
evidence.note: Al-Furūʿ states for the parallel case of two slaves that no manumission takes place while it remains unknown.
